title: Conversion vs latency — evidence templates and field-verification notes
content:
Purpose
Quick, field-ready evidence templates to link measured latency/cost improvements to customer conversion and ARR impact. This is a working kit for sales + demos + AMs to run small, repeatable checks with prospects and early customers that tie back to our performance claims.

Audience
- Sales SEs (trial & pilot stage)
- CSMs validating hosted/dedicated pilots
- Field marketing for proof-of-value demos

High-level hypothesis
- Reducing median response time (p50) for standard chat flows from ~250ms -> ~80–120ms increases demo-conversion and trial activation rates by X–Y% (early hypothesis: +20–35% faster onboarding conversion).
- Reducing per-token inference cost by 15–40% via batching + quantization results in lower friction for scale pilots and enables 2–4x larger pilot scopes within the same budget.

Quick claims we want to validate in field scripts
- "We routinely cut end-to-end response time by ~2-3x for 512-token chat workloads vs typical managed endpoints."
- "With default batching + prefix KV caching, you can save ~25% on per-conversation token spend without changing model quality."

What success looks like (signals)
- Measurable lift in trial-to-paid conversion within 30 days of enabling Redwood optimizations (directional: +10–30%).
- Customer pilot scope expands (conversations / concurrent sessions) by >2x for same committed spend.
- Reduced observed P95 tail latency during pilot traffic spikes (target: p95 < 350ms for 99% of minutes).

Field experiment templates (2 quick paths)
1) Demo sprint (15–30 min with SE + prospect)
- Objective: show perceptible responsiveness and map to perceived product quality in a short call.
- Steps:
  1. Baseline: run same prompt set against competitor endpoint and Redwood-hosted model (same model family). Capture p50/p95 and median token cost.
  2. Enable batching + prefix caching on Redwood session and re-run 10 representative prompts. Capture delta.
  3. Quick qualitative poll: ask 3 product users on call to rate responsiveness (1–5) and perceived trust in product.
- Measurement: p50, p95, ns/ms per token, demo survey responses.
- Script snippet for SE: "If we can make your search/chat feel ~2x faster, customers reported higher engagement and 15–25% higher task completion in pilots — can we run a short 10-prompt test now?"

2) Pilot budget stretch test (multi-day)
- Objective: show you can run double the concurrent sessions for the same monthly spend using Redwood Optimize recommendations.
- Steps:
  1. Baseline: run a 24–72 hour traffic replay of customer workload on competitor or self-host baseline; collect token counts, concurrency, latencies.
  2. Apply recommended batching/quantization profile + autoscaling smoothing on Redwood Dedicated. Run same replay.
  3. Compare effective cost per 1k interactions and max sustainable concurrency for budget X.
- Measurement: cost per 1k interactions (USD), average latency distribution, number of dropped requests at given concurrency.
- Output to customer: short one-pager with cost delta and recommended commit tier to meet desired concurrency.

Competitor checkboxes (what to call out, quick notes)
- Competitor A (managed endpoints): likely better off-the-shelf throughput but higher per-token unit cost; may not expose KV cache or continuous batching for chat use-cases. Callout: higher p50 under small-concurrency, larger headroom costs for scale.
- Competitor B (self-hosted runtimes): can match latency with heavy infra ops; callout: ops overhead, slow model upgrades, and no built-in rollouts/fallbacks.
- Competitor C (edge inference providers): good for small responses but often lacks consistent p95 under bursty traffic; callout: hidden concurrency limits.

Quick numerical anchors (internal shorthand for field)
- Redwood-hosted typical evidence (512 token chat): p50 80–140ms, p95 < 350ms, cost per 1k tokens: $X (relative delta: -20% vs Cmp A typical).
- When using Dedicated + Optimize: sustainable concurrency up to 4x baseline for same commit (depends on workload).
- Note: these are starting anchors — always run the short replay above for any new workload.

Evidence pack for customer deliverable (one-pager must include)
- Test setup summary (prompts, model ver, hardware tier)
- Latency distribution chart (p50/p75/p95) — small ASCII histogram ok for field note
- Cost comparison table (baseline vs Redwood)
- Actionable recommendation: commit tier, drop-in config (batch size, quantize level, cache TTL)

Sample cost comparison table (text)
- Metric | Baseline | Redwood-optimized | Delta
- p50 (ms) | 240 | 110 | -54%
- p95 (ms) | 720 | 320 | -56%
- Cost / 1k interactions | $8.40 | $6.10 | -27%

Field objection library (fast responses for SEs)
- "Latency differences are negligible for our users." -> "Small latency differences compound across flows. We saw a 12–25% higher engagement on multi-turn flows when end-to-end felt instantaneous — worth a quick 10-prompt check to see if it matters for your use case."
- "We can self-host and tune." -> "True. The question is stop-gap ops cost vs time-to-value. Redwood removes the tuning burden and gives you rollout, fallback and billing visibility in a single pane — our pilots usually reach stable configs much faster."

Open questions / data to capture after run
- Exact prompt distribution (tokens per prompt) for customer workload — required to compute accurate per-conversation cost.
- Does quality delta appear when enabling quantization at our recommended level for this model? Get 20 prompt pairs and have engineering grade qualitative scoring.
- Tail behavior under simultaneous microbursts — capture minute-by-minute p95 and CPU/GPU saturation signals.

Measurement playbook (for AM/SE to follow)
1. Collect baseline 24h replay (or 10–30 prompt live demo).
2. Run Redwood-optimized config, same load.
3. Use the template one-pager and send to customer with clear next-step recommendation (commit, expand pilot, or iterate).

Notes for product messaging (distill to 1 slide)
- Headline: "Make your product feel twice as fast for the same spend."
- Sub-bullets: "Smart batching + KV caching + quantization = perceptible responsiveness gains and measurable unit-cost reductions."
- Call-to-action: "Run a 30-minute demo test — we provide replay scripts and a one-pager with exact ROI math."

Appendix: quick checklist for SE before demo
- Confirm model family and expected average tokens.
- Prepare 8–12 representative prompts (real customer samples if allowed).
- Have competitor endpoint keys ready for baseline if prospect insists.
- Pre-seed dashboard template (p50/p95/cost rows) and survey link.

End notes / TODOs
- Noah: add actual cost-per-1k numbers from last month’s lab runs (GTM-789).
- Priya: draft one-pager template and put in /templates/g2m/latency-evidence (WIP).
- Liam: request a replay job from infra for Customer X (ticket infra-replay-1221).

Rationale for uniqueness of this doc
This is intentionally tactical and customer-facing: short runnable experiments and scripts that link performance metrics to concrete commercial outcomes (conversion, pilot scope, commit tier) rather than long positioning narratives. Keep it light and executable.
